contentFull:
What pig innovations are in the spotlight at EuroTier 2026?

More than ever before, swine innovations come at the speed of light, in 2026. After all, artificial intelligence (AI) is providing endless new opportunities and practical applications in the pig house. No wonder then, that a wide range of promising innovations including AI can be found at the upcoming edition of EuroTier 2026 in Hanover, Germany. In total, 13 innovations were awarded a medal: 2 gold and 11 silver. Here's what to look out for.

Vincent ter BeekEditor of Pig Progress / Topic: Pigs around the world

Sep 28

News

International visitors gather at the booth of Dutch flooring company Nooyen during EuroTier 2024. Photo: Mark Pasveer 

Smart farrowing pen

Photo: Weda

The Smart Farrowing Pen by German livestock equipment manufacturer Weda and supported by technology company Vetvise has grabbed one of the four gold medals in EuroTier 2026. The pen is a retrofittable, camera-based and AI-controlled assistance system. The innovation combines AI-supported analysis of the behaviour of sows and piglets with automated barn and feeding technology. Control variables, such as piglet nest temperature and feed curve, are adjusted independently and autonomously on the basis of real-time data. The innovation also was awarded a EuroTier Animal Welfare Award 2026. (Hall 17 B04)

Cleaning and removing manure

Photo: Peter Prinzing

The Pig-Barn-Cleaner by German company Peter Prinzing is an autonomous, fully automatic system for cleaning and removing manure from defined partial areas within each individual pen. The system automatically drives the animals out of the pen area with the aid of a pen partition wall. The area to be cleaned is then automatically cleaned with a cleaning unit based on a radial brush system. The manure is caught in a collecting tank and discharged at a transfer point. (Hall 12, D10)

Sensory concept

Photo: HealthTech BioActives

The product Weanex NEO by Spanish company HealthTech BioActives has won a silver medal. It fosters early solid feed consumption in piglets by mimicking natural olfactory signals from the placenta, colostrum and sow milk. The addition of neohesperidin dihydrochalcone also improves the tastiness of the feed while simultaneously masking the unpleasant tastes of other functional ingredients. This biologically inspired approach facilitates the transition from milk to solid feed, increases feed consumption and growth and improves the piglets’ development after weaning. (Hall 20, D14)

Biostimulation technology

Illustration: Solomon

ReproScent Series (No. 1, 3, 5), by the South Korean company Solomon, is a non-invasive biostimulation technology for pigs (also for cattle and goats). It is aimed at supplementing or replacing hormone injections by administering species-specific pheromones by means of room diffusers or sprays. The pheromones naturally stimulate the reproductive axis. The method improves fertilisation rates, reduces stress for the animals and simplifies operational procedures. (Hall 15, E23)

Supporting gut health

Photo: Vilofoss

The product In-Force S by Danish feed manufacturer Vilofoss supports the gut health of piglets in sensitive rearing stages, just after weaning. It consists of stabilised black soldier fly oil, which is rich in lauric acid, active ingredients and bitters extracted from hops and selected essential oils. Based on a practical powder technology, these complementary lipid and phytogenic components can be used in the form of a stable and precisely dosable product. Initial trials have shown a significant reduction in the microbial count as well as benefits in feed efficiency and animal health. (Hall 21, H16)

Fill level measuring using laser

Illustration: Constantec

More silver medal news from South Korea: Feed Check by the Korean company Constantec optimises fill level monitoring in feed silos by means of precise Lidar technology. That is a laser-based measurement technology, precisely registering the surface of the feed pile in the silo and enabling the remaining volume to be determined accurately. Integrated temperature and humidity sensors additionally monitor feed quality. With its long service life of up to 5 years, the rechargeable battery enables low-maintenance operation and increases process reliability. (Hall 12, B03)

Smart cleaning robot

Photo: MS Schippers

The MS Smart Cleaning Robot, introduced by MS Schippers from the Netherlands, automates barn cleaning in pig farming and combines chemical soaking, washing and disinfection in a single system. The robot uses 3D Lidar technology to navigate and clean areas that are difficult to access. The intelligent software can also recognise the differences between aisles and pens. The robot, which has a 5.50 m long, extendable washing arm, comes with a remote control. Recognising remaining dirt stains using photos and digital AI feedback could be a future addition. (Hall 11, E15)

Infrared heating system

Photo: ATX Suisse

The ATX AluXheat, showcased by Swiss company ATX Suisse, is an infrared heating system for pig rearing that has evolved specifically for sometimes challenging conditions in pig barns – think of moisture or gases. The system combines a sealed aluminium housing with energy-optimised infrared technology. Thanks to its IPX9-certified design, the heating element is resistant to high-pressure cleaners and the ingress of water is reliably prevented. (Hall 15, G19 and Hall 16, B02)

Reducing dust in the pig house

Photo: Schauer Agrotronic

Strohmatic Aero Dust Control by Austrian livestock equipment company Schauer Agrotronic reduces dust during straw distribution and extensively prevents dust from occurring. Thanks to a central, sensor-controlled oil dosing system, only a minimal amount of oil is used during the littering process. In the past, the dust problem was tackled by spraying oil directly into the pens. The novel solution, winning a silver medal this EuroTier, however, reduces consumption, cleaning effort and costs, and improves barn hygiene. (Hall 16, A04)

New generation feeding tank

Photo: Weda

German livestock equipment company Weda, once again, won a medal – this time a silver medal for the Weda QEW. This feeding tank is a member of a new generation of mixing vessels which integrates a generously dimensioned, pressure-resistant service hatch in the lower segment of the mixing vessel at floor level, eliminating what was a weakness in the maintenance and servicing of the mixing tanks. A large service hatch at floor level enables safe, direct access, while the newly designed agitator bearing can be replaced without heavy lifting work. (Hall 17, B04)

Slurry cassettes

Photo: Aco Funki

The SpaceKit Slurry Cassettes from Danish livestock equipment company Aco Funki reduce emissions from pig barns thanks to their funnel-shaped design, which results in a smaller slurry surface area and a shorter storage time. Ammonia, methane and odour emissions are effectively reduced in combination with an underfloor extraction system – something that was confirmed in initial comparative measurements in Denmark. The modular designs enables the system to be retrofitted into existing farms. It also improves animal welfare and working conditions. (Hall 15, D14)

AI supported management system

Illustration: VetVise

The BarnBuddy from German technology company VetVise is an AI-supported herd and health management system for pigs, poultry and cattle. Cameras analyse behaviour, activity and animal distribution, recognising problems early on. The system’s core element is a generative AI assistant that links complex data with veterinary medicine and agricultural science details and translates this locally into action recommendations – in 35 languages. (Hall 16, D23)

AI supported camera system

Photo: Weda

PigTail from Weda is an AI-supported, automated, camera-based image system for sorting gates in pig farming. It automatically assesses the tail condition of each pig and recognises indications of tail biting or necrosis early on. This enables the farmer to implement measures and provide more manipulation material or isolate susceptible animals even before systematic tail biting takes hold throughout the entire group. As the system continuously aggregates the data, it can instantly supply the exact number of animals with intact curly tails. (Hall 17, B04)

New housing concept

German livestock equipment company Big Dutchman presents Zone3, a flexible housing concept for piglet rearing and pig finishing. At the heart of this innovation is the patented arrangement of two longitudinal troughs, which are rotated by 90 degrees relative to the pen’s axis. This arrangement divides the pen into clearly separated areas for resting, eating and defecating, thus creating a stable functional structure that is the ideal choice for a wide variety of management types. The positioning of the trough ensures a low animal/feeding space ratio and a structural element within the pen. (Hall 17, D15)
translationZh:
2026年，猪业创新的速度比以往任何时候都快。毕竟，人工智能（AI）正在猪舍中提供无穷无尽的新机遇和实际应用。因此，在即将于德国汉诺威举行的EuroTier 2026上，将涌现大量包括AI在内的有前景的创新成果，也就不足为奇了。共有13项创新荣获奖牌：2枚金牌和11枚银牌。以下是值得关注的内容。

**智能产房**

由德国畜牧设备制造商Weda推出、技术公司Vetvise支持的智能产房（Smart Farrowing Pen）荣获了EuroTier 2026的四枚金牌之一。该产房是一套可改装、基于摄像头和AI控制的辅助系统。这项创新将AI支持的母猪和仔猪行为分析与自动化猪舍和饲喂技术相结合。仔猪巢温度、饲喂曲线等控制变量可根据实时数据独立自主地调整。该创新还获得了EuroTier 2026动物福利奖。（17号馆 B04）

**清洁与清粪**

由德国公司Peter Prinzing推出的Pig-Barn-Cleaner是一套自主全自动系统，用于清洁和清除每个猪栏内指定局部区域的粪便。该系统借助栏内隔墙自动将动物驱赶出猪栏区域，然后通过基于径向刷系统的清洁单元自动清洁待清理区域。粪便被收集到收集罐中，并在转运点排出。（12号馆 D10）

**感官概念**

西班牙公司HealthTech BioActives的产品Weanex NEO荣获银牌。该产品通过模拟胎盘、初乳和母猪乳汁的天然嗅觉信号，促进仔猪早期固体饲料的采食。添加新橙皮苷二氢查尔酮还能改善饲料的适口性，同时掩盖其他功能性成分的不良味道。这种受生物学启发的方法促进了从乳汁到固体饲料的过渡，提高了饲料消耗量和生长速度，并改善了仔猪断奶后的发育。（20号馆 D14）

**生物刺激技术**

韩国公司Solomon的ReproScent系列（1号、3号、5号）是一种用于猪（也适用于牛和山羊）的非侵入性生物刺激技术。其目标是通过室内扩散器或喷雾器施用物种特异性信息素，来补充或替代激素注射。信息素自然刺激生殖轴。该方法提高了受精率，减少了动物的应激，并简化了操作流程。（15号馆 E23）

**支持肠道健康**

丹麦饲料制造商Vilofoss的产品In-Force S支持仔猪在敏感饲养阶段（即断奶后）的肠道健康。该产品由稳定的黑水虻油组成，富含月桂酸、活性成分以及从啤酒花和精选精油中提取的苦味物质。基于实用的粉末技术，这些互补的脂质和植物源成分可以以稳定且精确可剂量的产品形式使用。初步试验显示微生物数量显著减少，并在饲料效率和动物健康方面有所改善。（21号馆 H16）

**激光料位测量**

更多来自韩国的银牌消息：韩国公司Constantec的Feed Check通过精确的激光雷达（Lidar）技术优化饲料筒仓的料位监测。这是一种基于激光的测量技术，能精确记录筒仓内饲料堆的表面，从而准确确定剩余体积。集成的温度和湿度传感器还可监测饲料质量。凭借长达5年的使用寿命，可充电电池实现了低维护运行并提高了过程可靠性。（12号馆 B03）

**智能清洁机器人**

由荷兰MS Schippers推出的MS智能清洁机器人将猪场的猪舍清洁自动化，将化学浸泡、清洗和消毒集成在一个系统中。该机器人使用3D激光雷达技术进行导航，清洁难以到达的区域。智能软件还能识别通道和猪栏之间的差异。该机器人配有一个5.50米长的可伸缩清洗臂，并附带遥控器。利用照片和数字AI反馈识别残留污渍可能是未来的附加功能。（11号馆 E15）

**红外加热系统**

由瑞士公司ATX Suisse展示的ATX AluXheat是一种用于养猪的红外加热系统，专门针对猪舍中有时颇具挑战性的条件进行了改进——比如潮湿或气体。该系统将密封铝制外壳与能源优化的红外技术相结合。得益于IPX9认证设计，加热元件耐高压清洗机，并能可靠防止水进入。（15号馆 G19和16号馆 B02）

**减少猪舍粉尘**

奥地利畜牧设备公司Schauer Agrotronic的Strohmatic Aero Dust Control在垫草分配过程中减少粉尘，并广泛防止粉尘产生。得益于中央传感器控制的油剂量系统，在垫草过程中仅使用极少量的油。过去，粉尘问题是通过直接向猪栏喷洒油来解决的。然而，这项在本次EuroTier上获得银牌的新颖解决方案降低了消耗、清洁工作和成本，并改善了猪舍卫生。（16号馆 A04）

**新一代饲喂罐**

德国畜牧设备公司Weda再次获奖——这次是Weda QEW获得的银牌。该饲喂罐是新一代混合容器的一员，在混合容器下部地面位置集成了一个尺寸宽大、耐压的检修口，消除了混合罐维护和保养方面的弱点。地面位置的大型检修口可实现安全、直接的进入，而新设计的搅拌器轴承无需重型起重作业即可更换。（17号馆 B04）

**粪浆槽**

丹麦畜牧设备公司Aco Funki的SpaceKit粪浆槽通过其漏斗形设计减少了猪舍排放，这种设计导致更小的粪浆表面积和更短的储存时间。与地下抽风系统结合使用时，氨气、甲烷和气味排放得到有效减少——丹麦的初步对比测量证实了这一点。模块化设计使该系统能够改装到现有农场中。它还改善了动物福利和工作条件。（15号馆 D14）

**AI支持的管理系统**

德国技术公司VetVise的BarnBuddy是一套AI支持的猪、禽和牛群健康管理系统。摄像头分析行为、活动和动物分布，及早识别问题。该系统的核心要素是一个生成式AI助手，它将复杂数据与兽医学和农业科学细节联系起来，并以35种语言在本地转化为行动建议。（16号馆 D23）

**AI支持的摄像头系统**

Weda的PigTail是一套AI支持的、自动化的、基于摄像头的图像系统，用于养猪中的分选门。它自动评估每头猪的尾部状况，及早识别咬尾或坏死的迹象。这使养殖户能够采取措施，提供更多的 manipulable material 或隔离易感动物，甚至在系统性咬尾在整个群体中蔓延之前。由于系统持续汇总数据，它可以即时提供拥有完整卷尾的动物的确切数量。（17号馆 B04）

**新型饲养概念**

德国畜牧设备公司Big Dutchman展示了Zone3，一种用于仔猪饲养和育肥的灵活饲养概念。这项创新的核心是两项纵向料槽的专利布局，它们相对于猪栏轴线旋转了90度。这种布局将猪栏划分为休息、采食和排泄的明确分离区域，从而创建了稳定的功能结构，是各种管理类型的理想选择。料槽的定位确保了较低的动物/采食空间比，并在猪栏内形成了结构元素。（17号馆 D15）
author: Vincent ter Beek
